A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work and 20 readable pages, including Appendices A–F. Text extraction and visual comparison cover the equations, algorithms, tables, and figures; the differences are limited to presentation.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation experiments, quantitative scores in Table 1, ablations in Figure 4, spectral analyses, and qualitative results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including Table 1, the ablations and spectral analyses, and the appendix generation examples.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same scalar-conditioning adapter, joint backbone LoRA training, and removal of shallow-block LoRA weights during inference. Figure 2's formatting adjustments do not change the architecture or procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic and photorealistic data for shutter speed, aperture, and color temperature. The evaluation prompts and Appendix F scenarios covering complex motion, depth layouts, and stylized scenes are unchanged.

E2.justification: Figure 5 retains WAN 2.1 prompting, Generative Photography, and Bokeh Diffusion in the same control-specific comparisons. The backbone baseline, clean/dirty inference variants, and joint/adapter-only training comparisons also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The protocols retain the one-scene/seven-condition comparison, 800-prompt FEP evaluation, and 96-prompt SVP evaluation with 50 denoising steps and 49 frames. Model configuration, metrics, sampling procedures, and training settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The data-complexity and inference-strategy ablations, spectral comparisons, backbone-corruption examples, and generalization analyses are identical. Sections 6–7 and Appendices D–F add or remove no analytical evidence.

E5.justification: Seed handling and uncertainty reporting are unchanged, including fixed-seed FEP generation and the different-seed backbone self-comparison in Section 5.1. No repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Table 1, plotted results, and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, baseline and ST(clean) X-CLIP scores remain 25.390 and 25.587. Figure 3 uses the identical underlying example images despite small display adjustments.

T1.justification: The SSF, SS-FD, drift-rate, and intruder-dimension definitions remain unchanged, as do the spectral-analysis procedures in Algorithms 2–3. No mathematical reasoning, derivation, assumption, or proof is added or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about learning physical controls from simple synthetic data while preserving backbone fidelity. The claimed factorized adaptation and evaluation contributions retain their original scope.

C2.justification: Both versions give identical explanations of factorization, catastrophic forgetting, and the adapter-only 'Bulldozer Effect.' Appendix D.2 retains the same limitation concerning residual artifacts under extreme controls after photorealistic-data training.

D1.justification: Appendices A–D retain identical data-generation instructions, pseudocode, hyperparameters, hardware, and training-time disclosures, including the Wan2.1-T2V-14B backbone and rank-32 LoRA. Code and data access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 57 bibliography entries are unchanged. Neither the cited works nor the positioning relative to controllable generation, synthetic-data learning, and video evaluation changes.

P1.justification: The narrative text and section structure remain unchanged. Surface edits include capitalizing 'shutter' as 'Shutter' in Figure 3 and updating the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

P2.justification: Figures 2 and 3 have small scaling, spacing, and label-placement adjustments while retaining their panels, captions, and image content. Tables and the remaining figures are unchanged; all appendix pages render identically.

improvement.justification: v3 preserves the methods, evidence, claims, limitations, and reproducibility information of v1. The small formatting adjustments in Figures 2–3 and updated version stamp do not materially improve or harm clarity, scientific support, or overall paper quality.
